Interface ChaosEffect

All Known Implementing Classes:

public sealed interface ChaosEffect permits ChaosEffect.DelayEffect, ChaosEffect.GateEffect, ChaosEffect.RejectEffect, ChaosEffect.SuppressEffect, ChaosEffect.ExceptionalCompletionEffect, ChaosEffect.ExceptionInjectionEffect, ChaosEffect.ReturnValueCorruptionEffect, ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect, ChaosEffect.SpuriousWakeupEffect, ChaosEffect.ErrnoEffect, ChaosEffect.ConnectionResetEffect, ChaosEffect.TrickleEffect, ChaosEffect.CorruptReadEffect, ChaosEffect.TimeoutEffect, ChaosEffect.TornWriteEffect, ChaosEffect.DnsAnswerEffect, ChaosEffect.DnsRewriteEffect, ChaosEffect.RedirectEffect, ChaosEffect.HeapPressureEffect, ChaosEffect.KeepAliveEffect, ChaosEffect.MetaspacePressureEffect, ChaosEffect.DirectBufferPressureEffect, ChaosEffect.GcPressureEffect, ChaosEffect.FinalizerBacklogEffect, ChaosEffect.DeadlockEffect, ChaosEffect.ThreadLeakEffect, ChaosEffect.ThreadLocalLeakEffect, ChaosEffect.MonitorContentionEffect, ChaosEffect.CodeCachePressureEffect, ChaosEffect.SafepointStormEffect, ChaosEffect.StringInternPressureEffect, ChaosEffect.ReferenceQueueFloodEffect, ChaosEffect.VirtualThreadCarrierPinningEffect
Describes the chaos behavior applied when a scenario matches an invocation.

Effects fall into two categories:

  • Interceptors — modify, delay, or terminate an in-flight JVM operation. Used with operation-targeted selectors (Thread, Executor, Method, etc.).
  • Stressors — active chaos that runs independently of any specific operation. Used exclusively with ChaosSelector.StressSelector.

Valid selector ↔ effect combinations are enforced by the runtime validator at activation time, not by the type system.

      static ChaosEffect.GateEffect gate(@Nullable Duration maxBlock)
      Returns a gate effect that blocks the matched operation until ChaosActivationHandle.release() is called or maxBlock elapses.

      Only the handle releases the gate, so a plan read from JSON (a plan file, HTTP, JMX or @WithChaos) must set maxBlock: the plan reader refuses a gate without one.

      Returns:
      a GateEffect that blocks for up to maxBlock

    • timeout

      static ChaosEffect.TimeoutEffect timeout()
      Returns an effect that lets the call time out: it waits for the socket's own timeout ( SO_TIMEOUT on a read, the connect timeout on a connect) and then throws SocketTimeoutException. It never fires when the timeout is infinite (0), like the native library's TIMEOUT. Valid for OperationType.SOCKET_READ and OperationType.SOCKET_CONNECT.
      Returns:
      a new ChaosEffect.TimeoutEffect

    • tornWrite

      static ChaosEffect.TornWriteEffect tornWrite()
      Returns an effect that tears a write: a FileChannel or SocketChannel write writes a random 1 to n-1 of the n bytes and returns that count, which callers must loop on; a socket stream write sends that prefix and then resets the connection. The native library's TORN. Valid for OperationType.FILE_IO_WRITE, OperationType.SOCKET_WRITE and OperationType.NIO_CHANNEL_WRITE; a file stream write (FileOutputStream, RandomAccessFile) either completes or throws, so a match there does nothing and counts no application.
      Returns:
      a new ChaosEffect.TornWriteEffect

    • suppress

      static ChaosEffect.SuppressEffect suppress()
      Returns a suppress effect that skips the matched operation. Where the call can be skipped the caller sees no exception and receives null, false, 0 or nothing, depending on the operation. Where skipping cannot be expressed the call fails instead: a thread start (THREAD_START, VIRTUAL_THREAD_START) throws RejectedExecutionException and SYSTEM_EXIT_REQUEST throws SecurityException.
      Returns:
      a SuppressEffect

    • injectException

      static ChaosEffect.ExceptionInjectionEffect injectException(String exceptionClassName, String message)
      Returns an exception injection effect that throws an instance of exceptionClassName at the entry of matched methods, before the method body executes. Only valid with ChaosSelector.MethodSelector and OperationType.METHOD_ENTER.

      The class must be in a java. or javax. package (IllegalArgumentException here) and is resolved at activation (ChaosValidationException for a class the agent cannot load or build); see ChaosEffect.ExceptionInjectionEffect. The exception is instantiated via reflection for each call. Both checked exceptions and Error subclasses are thrown as they are, by a sneaky throw that the compiler cannot check.

      With stack trace enabled (the default here), the exception carries a stack trace starting at the intercepted method. Use ExceptionInjectionEffect(String, String, boolean) directly with withStackTrace=false to throw it with an empty stack trace (the constructor still fills it; it is cleared before the throw).

      Parameters:
      exceptionClassName - binary class name of the exception type (e.g., "java.io.IOException"); must be a valid binary class name
      message - the exception message passed to the constructor; must be non-blank
      Returns:
      an ExceptionInjectionEffect

    • corruptReturnValue

      static ChaosEffect.ReturnValueCorruptionEffect corruptReturnValue(ChaosEffect.ReturnValueStrategy strategy)
      Returns a return value corruption effect that replaces the actual return value of matched methods on exit. Only valid with ChaosSelector.MethodSelector and OperationType.METHOD_EXIT.

      If the strategy is inapplicable to the actual return type (e.g., ChaosEffect.ReturnValueStrategy.EMPTY on a primitive), the runtime falls back to ChaosEffect.ReturnValueStrategy.ZERO and reports the substitution via the observability bus.

      Parameters:
      strategy - the substitution strategy to apply
      Returns:
      a ReturnValueCorruptionEffect

    • skewClock

      static ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect skewClock(Duration skewAmount, ChaosEffect.ClockSkewMode mode)
      Returns a clock skew effect that offsets or distorts the JVM clock as observed through System.currentTimeMillis() and System.nanoTime(). Only valid with ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector.

      The skew is applied in the instrumentation advice layer and does not affect the OS clock or other processes.

      Parameters:
      skewAmount - the clock offset to apply; positive = future, negative = past; must not be zero, except for FREEZE, where zero stops the clock at the moment the scenario starts
      mode - how the skew evolves over time
      Returns:
      a ClockSkewEffect

      Only valid with ChaosSelector.NioSelector and OperationType.NIO_SELECTOR_SELECT as its only operation.

      Returns:
      a SpuriousWakeupEffect

      Use with ChaosSelector.StressSelector targeting ChaosSelector.StressTarget.KEEPALIVE.

      threadName - name of the kept-alive thread; must be non-blank
      daemon - false prevents JVM shutdown until the handle is closed
      heartbeat - interval between keep-alive park cycles; must be positive
      Returns:
      a KeepAliveEffect

    • metaspacePressure

      static ChaosEffect.MetaspacePressureEffect metaspacePressure(int generatedClassCount, int fieldsPerClass)
      Returns a metaspace pressure stressor that generates and loads generatedClassCount synthetic classes with fieldsPerClass fields each, retaining strong references to prevent unloading. Simulates classloader leaks common in hot-deployment frameworks.

      Use with ChaosSelector.StressSelector targeting ChaosSelector.StressTarget.METASPACE.

      Parameters:
      generatedClassCount - number of synthetic classes to generate; must be > 0
      fieldsPerClass - instance fields per class (controls per-class metaspace footprint); must be >= 0
      Returns:
      a MetaspacePressureEffect

      static ChaosEffect.DirectBufferPressureEffect directBufferPressure(long totalBytes, int bufferSizeBytes)
      Returns a direct buffer pressure stressor that allocates off-heap direct ByteBuffers and retains them, simulating NIO/Netty buffer leaks. The buffers are held until the scenario stops, which releases them.

      Use with ChaosSelector.StressSelector targeting ChaosSelector.StressTarget.DIRECT_BUFFER.

      Parameters:
      totalBytes - total bytes of native memory to exhaust; must be > 0
      bufferSizeBytes - size of each individual buffer allocation; must be > 0 and <= totalBytes

      a DirectBufferPressureEffect

      static ChaosEffect.FinalizerBacklogEffect finalizerBacklog(int objectCount, Duration finalizerDelay)
      Returns a finalizer backlog stressor that creates objectCount objects with slow finalizers sleeping for finalizerDelay each. This backs up the finalizer thread queue, delaying GC reclamation and eventually causing OOM conditions.

      Returns a deadlock stressor that permanently deadlocks participantCount threads using ChaosEffect.DeadlockEffect.DEFAULT_ACQUISITION_DELAY between lock steps. The deadlock is released when the ChaosActivationHandle is closed.

      static ChaosEffect.ThreadLeakEffect threadLeak(int threadCount, String namePrefix, boolean daemon)
      Returns a thread leak stressor that spawns threadCount threads that never terminate. When daemon=false and the handle is not closed before JVM shutdown, the leaked threads will prevent clean JVM exit.

      static ChaosEffect.ThreadLocalLeakEffect threadLocalLeak(int entriesPerThread, int valueSizeBytes)
      Returns a ThreadLocal leak stressor that plants entriesPerThread × the common pool's parallelism ThreadLocal entries of valueSizeBytes each in threads from the common pool, simulating large request-scoped objects retained across requests in a pool thread. The pool spreads the entries over its workers.

      Parameters:

      valueSizeBytes - size of each entry's byte-array value; must be > 0
      Returns:
      a ThreadLocalLeakEffect

      static ChaosEffect.MonitorContentionEffect monitorContention(Duration lockHoldDuration, int contendingThreadCount)
      Returns a monitor contention stressor that spawns contendingThreadCount threads competing for a single lock held for lockHoldDuration each cycle, using fair lock ordering (FIFO). For a more destructive starvation scenario, use the full ChaosEffect.MonitorContentionEffect constructor with unfair=true.

      Parameters:
      lockHoldDuration - how long each thread holds the lock per cycle; must be positive
      contendingThreadCount - number of threads competing for the lock; must be >= 2
      Returns:
      a MonitorContentionEffect

    • codeCachePressure

      static ChaosEffect.CodeCachePressureEffect codeCachePressure(int classCount, int methodsPerClass)
      Returns a code-cache pressure stressor that generates and loads classCount synthetic classes, each with methodsPerClass methods, forcing JIT compilation to fill the JVM code cache. Once full, JIT compilation stops and the JVM falls back to interpreter mode, causing severe performance degradation (10–50× slowdown) with no exceptions thrown.

      Use with ChaosSelector.StressSelector targeting ChaosSelector.StressTarget.CODE_CACHE_PRESSURE.

      Parameters:
      classCount - number of synthetic classes to generate; must be > 0
      methodsPerClass - methods per class; must be > 0
      Returns:
      a CodeCachePressureEffect

      Parameters:
      gcInterval - interval between forced GC calls; must be positive
      Returns:
      a SafepointStormEffect

      static ChaosEffect.ReferenceQueueFloodEffect referenceQueueFlood(int referenceCount, Duration floodInterval)
      Returns a reference-queue flood stressor that creates referenceCount WeakReference objects every floodInterval, makes their referents unreachable, and triggers GC, flooding the ReferenceHandler thread's queue.

    • virtualThreadCarrierPinning

      static ChaosEffect.VirtualThreadCarrierPinningEffect virtualThreadCarrierPinning(int pinnedThreadCount, Duration pinDuration)
      Returns a virtual-thread carrier pinning stressor that starts pinnedThreadCount virtual threads, each of which holds its carrier for pinDuration per cycle: on JDK 21–23 by sleeping inside a synchronized block (true pinning, no CPU), on JDK 24 and later, where synchronized no longer pins (JEP 491), by spin-waiting (one CPU per held carrier). Without allowDestructiveEffects it leaves one carrier free.

      When a virtual thread is mounted on a carrier platform thread and that carrier enters a synchronized block, the JVM (JDK 21) "pins" the virtual thread to its carrier: the virtual thread cannot be unmounted until the synchronized block exits, even if it calls a blocking operation. The pinned carrier is therefore unavailable to run other virtual threads. This stressor replicates that condition by deliberately holding carriers inside synchronized blocks, reducing the effective carrier-thread pool size and causing virtual-thread starvation under load.

      Use with ChaosSelector.StressSelector targeting ChaosSelector.StressTarget.VIRTUAL_THREAD_CARRIER_PINNING.

      Parameters:
      pinnedThreadCount - number of carrier threads to pin; must be > 0
      pinDuration - how long each thread holds the pin per cycle; must be positive
      Returns:
      a VirtualThreadCarrierPinningEffect
